newsitem.title: CHINA: China to restructure coal industry, boost exports.
newsitem.headline: China to restructure coal industry, boost exports.

text.p: China will streamline its coal industry this year, merging major companies into more efficient groups to boost exports by the world's largest coal producer, state media said Sunday.

The restructuring is seen boosting exports to 40 million metric tons a year by the end of the century, up from 30 million tons in 1996, the China Daily Business Weekly said, quoting Wang Changchun, president of the China National Coal Import and Export Corp.
China's coal output was estimated at 1.35 billion tons in 1996, up 4.6 percent from the previous year, making it the world's biggest coal producer.

China would gather 14 state-owned coal firms into four groups to boost the competitiveness of an industry that is being forced to learn to compete in China's fledgling sink-or-swim market economy, the business weekly said.
The groups would be responsible for trade, use of coal, construction and equipment manufacturing, it said.
The first group, the China Coal Industry Import and Export Group, will be formed in April, but the timetable for forming the other groups has not been decided. it said.
The umbrella groups formed after the restructuring would control shares of their subsidiaries and share in the profits, the newspaper said.

China's coal industry is chronically inefficient, and of China's 93 key state-owned coal mines, only 55 were profitable last year. That was still more than double the 26 that were profitable in 1995, officials have said.
China has said it will open at least 300 coal projects to foreign investors, although it has not said whether investors could export output.
